conviction_note: Near non-result. The Q3 number is pinned by a $13.0-14.0m guide that the company has beaten in five straight quarters, so a small revenue beat is likely (+3% vs bar). The stock fell after four of those five beats and after five of its last six prints, the put skew is +10 vol points, and the print turns on the Q4 guide (consensus $15.1m) and 800V/2027 ramp timing, where I found no unpriced company number. Peer prints (MPWR 10-29, onsemi 11-02) are a positive AI-power read, but small for a company whose AI share is about a third of a $15m quarter. Shorts rose to 51.1m shares (about 19% of shares outstanding) into the print, which pulls p_up toward 50. Scaled: abs 14 x (2 x 0.46 - 1) = -1.12. Findings sum: -0.5. Both lean slightly negative and neither is far from zero.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue $13.5m: the company guide is $13.0-14.0m (8-K ex 99.1, 2026-07-27, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001821769/000162828026049795/exhibit991-navitassemicond.htm). Consensus is $13.43-13.5m: Benzinga lists $13.5m and EPS -$0.05 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NVTS/earnings-forecasts), and TIKR lists $13.50m Q3 and $15.10m Q4 (https://www.tikr.com/blog/navitas-stock-is-down-26-since-september-30-time-to-sell-or-load-up, 2026-10-20). Benzinga's Korean page still shows a stale $11.1m, which predates the July guide. Two agreeing sources plus the guide, so the bar is sourced. Non-GAAP GM guide 39.7% +/-100bp; non-GAAP opex $15.5-17.5m. The company said Q4 would grow double digits sequentially (at least ~$14.85m), so the Q4 consensus of $15.1m sits at the low end of that.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest via Equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/nvts/shortinterest): 51,056,584 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, up from 47.5m on 09-30 and 40.3m on 09-15; days to cover 2.82. Equibles states it as 27.8% of a stale 183m share count. Against about 268m shares (261.1m at 2026-07-24 per TIKR, plus about 6.9m Claros shares) it is about 19% of shares outstanding and higher as a share of float. The 10-30 settlement is not yet published. Options (baseline): 25d skew +10.21 vol points, so downside protection is bid. Put/call OI is 0.41, so open interest is call-heavy. Event-implied move 11.25%, straddle 13.31%. Tape: -26.3% over 20 days, -72% from the 52-week high of $34 on 2026-06-03, 20-day realised vol 97%. The short is crowded and building, and the skew agrees with a negative lean.

findings.finding: Navitas beat revenue consensus in each of its last five quarters, Q2 2026 at $10.53m against $9.97m, yet fell the next session after four of the five. The baseline shows five of six prints down, median absolute move 14.1%, including -12.27% after the Q2 beat with a raised Q3 guide. With the Q3 guide at $13.0-14.0m and consensus at the $13.5m midpoint, a revenue beat of about 3-5% is the market's own expectation, and on this name such a beat has been sold.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-27): revenue beat ($10.53m vs $9.97m) and a Q3 guide well above the street's $11.1m, stock -12.27%. Q1 2026 (05-05): beat ($8.6m vs $8.2m), -4.96%. Q4 2025 (02-24): +19.61%, the only up print in six.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The +10 vol-point put skew and the 26% slide since Sep 30 already show the market expects a sold beat. If it were fully priced, the call-heavy OI (put/call 0.41) and a 19% short position building into the print would not both be present. The open element is the reaction function, not the number.
findings.independence: The baseline's own reaction history (5 of 6 down, sealed from 8-K item 2.02 times) is a different source from TIKR's consensus-beat count and agrees. Benzinga's estimate table (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NVTS/earnings-forecasts) shows the same beat pattern of roughly 5-6% per quarter.

findings.finding: Two AI-power peers reported after Navitas last spoke on 2026-07-27, and both were strong on AI data centres. Monolithic Power (2026-10-29): Enterprise Data revenue $506.7m, +33.2% q/q and +164.6% y/y, data-centre growth floor raised to 150% from 130%, stock about +10% after hours. onsemi (2026-11-02): AI data-centre revenue +39% q/q and +175% y/y, and it raised its 2030 AI-DC target. Navitas guided AI infrastructure to about one-third of Q4 sales.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Navitas's moves on AI and Nvidia news have been large and positive (May-June 2026 rally to $34), but the earnings reactions to the AI narrative have been negative on 5 of 6 prints, so the transmission at prints is weak.
findings.why_not_priced: NVTS fell 5.6% over the five sessions that include the MPWR print and onsemi's release, so its price did not take the read-through. If it had, NVTS would have tracked MPWR's after-hours move rather than sitting at a 26% 20-day drawdown. Net of the rest of the company: Navitas's AI revenue is about $4-5m of a roughly $15m Q4, its big ramps (800V sidecars and compute trays) are dated mid-2027 by its own deck, and the other two-thirds is industrial, energy and remaining consumer. This is a peer proxy, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: onsemi 8-K ex 99.1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001097864/000114036126041580/ef20084671_ex99-1.htm, 2026-11-02) is a separate company and a separate document pointing the same way. Both are proxies, not Navitas numbers.

findings.finding: Monolithic Power said on 2026-10-29 that it began sampling GaN-based products for 800V data-centre architectures alongside its SiC designs. That puts a $1.2bn-a-quarter power supplier into the GaN-for-800V niche that anchors Navitas's thesis, beside Innoscience, which is on Nvidia's 800V partner list and has a signed Google supply agreement (Feb 2026).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No print has turned on competition explicitly. The 2026-10-16 move of -9.6% (vs SOX -3.8%) was attributed by commentary to Chinese competition among other things.
findings.why_not_priced: The MPWR GaN-sampling line was buried in a print the street read as an AI-demand beat; no Navitas coverage I found linked them. If it were priced, call Q&A previews would carry it. It reaches the stock only through the call Q&A and share-of-socket questions, so it is small.
findings.independence: Innoscience in Nvidia's 800V list and in Google's supply chain (https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/02/09/news-innoscience-gan-products-break-into-googles-supply-chain/, 2026-02-09) is a different source with the same direction, but it is older and widely known.

findings.finding: Short interest climbed 27% in a month into the print: 40.3m shares (Sep 15), then 47.5m (Sep 30), then 51.1m (Oct 15), about 19% of about 268m shares outstanding, with days to cover 2.8. A short this crowded and building into a binary print adds squeeze fuel if the Q4 guide or 2027 ramp language surprises. The Q4 2025 print squeezed +19.6%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Feb 2026 print: +19.61% with about 25-32% of float short at the time (per Trefis and other trackers). The other five prints all fell despite similar short interest.
findings.why_not_priced: The October build appears in no preview I found, and the baseline does not carry short interest. The sign is ambiguous: the build is also informed bearish positioning, which the skew already reflects. It is filed as a small net positive for the squeeze mechanism only.
findings.independence: Call-heavy open interest in the baseline (put/call 0.41) is consistent with a crowded short hedged with calls. It comes from a different source (Yahoo options).

findings.finding: At Citi's conference on 2026-09-08, CEO Chris Allexandre described the 800V transition as four stages and 'not a digital switch'. His own July deck dates 800V sidecars to mid-2027 and native 800V compute trays to mid/late 2027 into 2028. So the Q4 and 2027 commentary on the call is likelier to stretch timing than to pull it forward, which is the line this stock trades on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 call (2026-07-27): the guide was raised, the ramp was framed as 2H26-2027, and the stock fell 12.27%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The 26% fall since Sep 30 and the -72% from the June high already reflect a slower ramp. What would still be new is a quantified slip, such as AI share in Q4 below the one-third promised. I found no document showing it, so this is sized small.
findings.independence: The July investor deck (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001821769/000162828026049795/exhibit992-navitas2q26ea.htm) carries the same staged timeline, so the two share the company as source.

findings.finding: Navitas carries two active suits that can show up in Q3 opex and call Q&A. Renesas sued for trade-secret misappropriation and named CEO Allexandre personally (N.D. Cal. 5:26-cv-07573, 2026-07-22). Wolfspeed sued for patent infringement over GaNFast, GaNSlim, GaNSafe, GeneSiC MOSFETs and SiCPAK (D. Del., 2026-07-07). Navitas countersued Renesas in E.D. Tex. on 2026-08-10.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The suits were part of the July-August drawdown, per TIKR. No print has carried a legal-cost line.
findings.why_not_priced: The suits are public and priced. What is unpriced is the size of the legal spend, which is likely excluded from non-GAAP. No ruling falls in the window, so this is a below-the-line, call-Q&A item sized at a fraction.
findings.independence: Wolfspeed suit: https://www.iam-media.com/article/wolfspeed-sues-navitas-patent-infringement-over-gallium-nitride-and-silicon-carbide-technologies (separate article, same litigation cluster).

findings.finding: The Claros acquisition (integrated voltage regulators; up to $232.8m, about 6.9m shares or $89.7m at closing, plus an earnout capped at about 1.28m shares) closed on 2026-10-06. Management does not expect Claros revenue before about 2028. Its engineering cost therefore lands in the Q4 non-GAAP opex guide, last set at $15.5-17.5m for Q3, with no offsetting revenue, so the Q4 loss guide is likely wider than a pre-deal model.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print carried an acquisition opex step-up. EPS has been beaten only 2 of the last 8 quarters by one source's count, and the stock trades on revenue and AI narrative more than on opex.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q4 EPS consensus may not include Claros's run-rate, since estimates were set around the July guide. If it were in, Q4 EPS estimates would have moved after Oct 6, and I found no revision. It lands below revenue on a stock that trades on revenue and narrative, so it is small.
findings.independence: The deal terms are in the 2026-08-25 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001821769/000110465926100478/tm2623854d1_8k.htm), the same company as source. TIKR's '2028-2029' Claros revenue timing (https://www.tikr.com/blog/navitas-is-up-12-in-2026-73-off-its-high-is-the-power-wall-pitch-a-buy) is secondary.

findings.finding: Navitas holds $557.4m of cash (2026-06-30) against non-GAAP operating burn of roughly $9-10m a quarter, after $380.7m of ATM sales in May-June at about $22 average. There is no financing need at this print, so the dilution overhang that marked earlier prints is absent. Since July, the money has been spent on Claros (mostly stock), a $5m Magnachip stake (SiC licensing partner, 8-K 2026-09-21), and TSMC buffer inventory secured through 2029+.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The May-June ATM sales took place during the run to $34 and the subsequent unwind; prints themselves have not carried an offering.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It is filed because the question of what the money buys was asked and answered. The cash funds capacity (TSMC buffer, GF 8-inch GaN) and M&A, not distress, so the sign is a small positive. No ATM is needed in the window.
findings.independence: Magnachip 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001821769/000110465926109125/tm2625807d1_8k.htm, 2026-09-21) and TIKR's ATM figures (https://www.tikr.com/blog/navitas-is-up-12-in-2026-73-off-its-high-is-the-power-wall-pitch-a-buy) are separate documents.

outside_window.finding: The Renesas, Wolfspeed and Navitas patent and trade-secret cases have no ruling or hearing dated inside the window; any injunction risk on GaN or SiC product lines resolves later.
800V sidecar and compute-tray revenue is dated mid-2027 to 2028 by the company's own Q2 deck, and the 1200V SiC JFET line early 2027.

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR submissions since 2026-07-20 (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001821769.json): no 8-K after 2026-10-06, so no pre-announcement, no new financing and no leadership change before the print. The latest Form 4s are dated 2026-08-26 (a cluster of 8, not opened), and there are none in Sep-Oct.
The CEO letter of 2026-10-06 (8-K ex 99.2) has no Q3 trend, backlog, bookings or guidance reaffirmation.
Claros webinar of 2026-10-20: no transcript or coverage of any revenue or ramp remark found.
Analyst actions in Oct-Nov 2026: none found dated. MarketBeat average target $14.74 across 8 analysts, 5 Hold and 1 Sell per TIKR; Morgan Stanley Sell $12.60 is undated.
Catalyst for the 2026-10-27 +11% day: none found; TIKR names no cause.
Nvidia GTC or 800V timing updates in Oct 2026: none found beyond Navitas's own 24 kW board release (Oct 12).
Power Integrations Q3 2026: not yet reported as of the search; its Q2 call put 800V main-path revenue at 2028+.
Q2 2026 10-Q (customer concentration, inventory, ATM capacity): EDGAR returned 404 on both URL forms, not read.
GaN price competition data (Infineon, TI, Innoscience price cuts): no dated 2026 source found.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Benzinga Korean page Q3 revenue consensus of $11.1m, which would imply a large beat against the guide.
rejected_candidates.detail: That is the pre-guide Q2-era figure (247wallst quotes $11.1m as the pre-report Q3 consensus on 2026-07-27). The company guide of $13.0-14.0m (8-K 2026-07-27) and two current sources at $13.43-13.5m supersede it.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Eugene Sheridan sold 600,000 shares at $7.94 (quantisnow listing).
rejected_candidates.detail: The aggregator gives no date and Sheridan is no longer CEO (Allexandre is); EDGAR shows no Form 4 after 2026-08-26, so it cannot be dated into the run-up.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Navitas 24 kW board with Nvidia (Oct 12), Microchip 800V reference design (Oct 5), U.S. Army 10 kV SiC selection (Sep 28) as positive catalysts.
rejected_candidates.detail: These are product and partnership releases with no disclosed revenue, already part of the AI-power narrative in finding 2 and the 800V-timing finding 5. The stock fell through all of them.

baseline_tension: The findings agree with the put skew and the 26% 20-day drawdown: beats get sold and the ramp timing is long. The building short and the strong peer prints are the only things cutting against them, so the lean is mildly negative and close to zero rather than against the skew.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (crowded short, about 19% of shares and rising): negatives shrunk once. 800V timing -0.5 to -0.3, litigation -0.3 to -0.2, Claros opex -0.4 to -0.3. p_up 45 to 46.
Rule 5 (proxy smaller than company numbers): MPWR GaN-competition finding -0.5 to -0.4.
Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): peer AI read-through +1.0 to +0.8, because AI is about one-third of a $15m Q4 and the large ramps are 2027.
Rule 1 left the reaction-history finding at -0.8 (it already carried the reaction veto) and print_vs_bar at +3.0.
Rule 8 / core (guidance likely moves, the name's median reaction 14.1%): abs_move_pct 13 to 14.
Rule 4: the financing finding was already signed after asking what the money buys; unchanged at +0.2.
